overview.text: Today's key developments highlight critical advances in infrastructure, security, and research methodologies across the artificial intelligence landscape. OpenAI detailed how it strengthened containment for frontier model training and evaluation through offline environments and high-compute red-teaming. In hardware and systems, new community discoveries unlocked instruction issue rates on Nvidia cards, while analysis explored the symbiosis between Huawei hardware and DeepSeek. In research, new work investigated the provenance of specific tokens in reasoning models and introduced agentic systems for virtual film cinematography alongside explainable artifact detection for generated videos. Additionally, Ai2 released LitPivot to help researchers dynamically contextualize ideas within literature landscapes, and educational resources emerged covering the construction of custom reasoning models through inference-time scaling and reinforcement learning.

entries.summary: Complex camera motion is central to visual storytelling, yet translating cinematographic intent into controllable, executable camera trajectories remains challenging.

entries.summary: Recent advances in video generation have made synthetic videos increasingly realistic, placing greater demands on reliable AI-generated video detection.
entries.why: Improves reliable detection methods for increasingly realistic synthetic and generated videos.

entries.title: Inherited, Not Invented: Tracing the Provenance of Wait in Reasoning Models
entries.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is credited with teaching reasoning models to write {wait} before reconsidering a step, yet large RL accuracy gains do not require the word. This view can confuse what RL discovers with what a model inherits from its training data.
entries.why: Clarifies the distinction between reinforcement learning discoveries and data inheritance in reasoning models.
